question: When references go missing, how wrong are the inferred abundances p and interior positions x -- separately from the count collapse of stage 288?

design.removal_convention: observations are removed; the reference tree keeps every edge (stage 288 variant B)
design.baseline: level "none" is the full panel, the no-loss reference point

arms.fibre_true: exact fibre over the true support given the retained data; LP bounds in Fractions, suprema over the closure
arms.fibre_found: the same over the support the exact solver returned, when different
arms.dd_default: DecoDiPhy 1.5.0 defaults, k by its own stopping rules

design.wasserstein: reusing stage289_headtohead_analyze.wasserstein together with point_distances: balanced optimal transport between the recovered and generating mixtures under the tree metric, computed in the analysis step so the stage 289 numbers are directly comparable
design.decodiphy_tuning: none; documented defaults, only the k control named in the arm
design.decodiphy_missing_references: DecoDiPhy handles missing references itself: preprocess_input prunes leaves absent from the distance file and contracts their parents, and post_process_output maps placements back to the original tree. Its jplace writer (cli.py:384) then looks those anchors up in the PRUNED tree and can raise KeyError; all_rounds.json is already written at cli.py:379, so this stage reads the placements the tool itself committed and records jplace_writer_crashed. No refit, no tuning, no fallback method.

predictions: H1 the abundance error grows with the removed fraction and is worse under the structured regimes, mirroring the count collapse of stage 288.

H2 a retained, CORRECT support can still carry large abundance error, because the fibre over the true support gains free parameters as references are removed; this is a separate effect from the count collapse.
H3 positive-dimensional fibres are not rare and their diameters are large enough that a single reported p is not a well-defined quantity.
H4 no prediction is registered for which of the exact method and the heuristic degrades more gracefully.
